title: Security posture discovery - Redwood & Apollo Biotech
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Head of IT, Apollo), Dr. Marcus Velez (CTO), Priya Singh (Security Engineer)

Summary: short discovery on security posture and deployment options for regulated life-sciences workloads.

-- Topics / Agenda --
- Quick intros (5m)
- Compliance posture: SOC2/ISO (10m)
- Auth/identity: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC (10m)
- Logs, retention, encryption/KMS (10m)
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private, networking (10m)
- Next steps & action items (5m)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our solutions engineer. How's it going?
[00:08] Sara Patel: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Good, thanks- appreciate you making time. Marcus just joined a sec.
[00:12] Dr. Marcus Velez: Sorry about that, ran a bit over. Marcus here.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: No worries. We'll do a quick run-through of security posture items you sent over and answer questions.
[00:22] Priya Singh: Great. We're mainly evaluating whether we can use Redwood Hosted for initial workloads or if we need Dedicated / Private right away because of data residency and ePHI concerns.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Totally understood. Maybe quick question: what's the rough classification of the data you expect to send - PHI, de-identified, research notes?
[00:38] Sara Patel: It's a mix. The POC will touch de-identified patient notes and some metadata that could be considered PHI under certain linkages. So from a compliance standpoint we need to assume it's sensitive.
[00:47] Liam O'Connor: Okay that helps. We'll walk through our SOC2, ISO status and then the deployment options. For context, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we also have an ISO 27001 attestation - the most recent reports are in the security pack we'll share.
[01:03] Priya Singh: When you say SOC2 Type II, does that cover the hosted service and your subproc vendors? We need to confirm vendor scope, right?
[01:12] Maya Chen: Good question. Our SOC2 covers our hosted control plane and core inference runtime as a service. The report includes a list of subservice organizations - cloud infra, monitoring, etc. We'll include the subservice list in the pack.
[01:26] Dr. Marcus Velez: Do you do annual pen tests and have an external pen-test summary we can review?
[01:31] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we have yearly third-party penetration tests and internal vulnerability scans. We include high-level findings in the pen test summary - we don't publish full exploit details but we'll share remediation evidence where possible.
[01:42] Sara Patel: Okay. On identity - we use Okta SAML + SCIM for provisioning. We need SSO and automated user provisioning, plus fine-grained RBAC so we can enforce least privilege across teams.
[01:55] Maya Chen: Right - Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For RBAC we have role templates and you can map to SAML attributes. There is also API-level RBAC for service keys, and scoped keys for model access.
[02:10] Priya Singh: Any gotchas we should be aware of? For example, can we enforce session timeouts, conditional access?
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: Session policy hooks are supported via SAML and you can also set short-lived tokens for automation. For conditional access, we rely on the IdP for device/compliance checks - we don't proxy that in our hosted flow.
[02:29] Dr. Marcus Velez: For Dedicated and Private options, is SAML still supported?
[02:33] Maya Chen: Yes, both Dedicated and Private support SAML and SCIM. With Private, since it's in your VPC or on-prem, you can integrate directly with internal IdPs or LDAP.
[02:44] Sara Patel: On encryption - are keys customer-managed? We want KMS integration and ideally HSM-backed keys for certain datasets.
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: For Hosted, we offer CMK via cloud KMS (customers provision keys in their cloud account and we use them for data encryption in transit and rest). We also support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments where the customer manages the HSM. For Dedicated we can discuss bring-your-own-key via a delegated KMS model.
[03:10] Priya Singh: So hosted can do CMK but key material stays with the cloud provider, correct? We need to ensure Redwood doesn't have plaintext access to keys.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Correct - with CMK customer controls key access. We do not retain plaintext keys. We'll include a KMS integration diagram in the pack.
[03:25] Sara Patel: Audit logs - what do you capture and how long are they retained? We need tenant-level audit trails with immutable logs for 7 years potentially.
[03:34] Liam O'Connor: We capture request-level logs, actor identity, IPs, model used, token counts, and metadata. Default retention in hosted is 90 days, but for Dedicated and Private you can configure retention and export to your SIEM. We also support log streaming to your S3 or GCS.
[03:50] Priya Singh: Is the audit log tamper-evident? Any append-only or WORM features?
[03:54] Liam O'Connor: For Hosted, we provide signed audit records and can integrate with an append-only store in customer cloud using object lock. Private deployments can use your existing immutability controls. We'll add details and examples.
[04:06] Dr. Marcus Velez: Data residency - we need processing to occur in the EU for certain projects. Are there EU regions for Hosted?
[04:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we have EU-hosted regions and can guarantee region-bound processing for hosted customers. For Dedicated we can provision capacity in a specific region; Private obviously runs in your environment.
[04:22] Sara Patel: What about data retention for prompts and generated outputs? We have a policy to avoid retaining any PII beyond processing window unless explicitly allowed.
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: By default, request data is transient. For Hosted we offer options: ephemeral-only (no storage), short-term cache for performance, or persistent storage if you enable logging. We can set retention windows per project. For stricter use cases we'd recommend Dedicated or Private with explicit retention configurations.
[04:49] Priya Singh: Do you support tokenization or partial redaction for logs?
[04:53] Maya Chen: We have an anonymization pipeline you can enable that strips PII before storage; it's part of Redwood Optimize add-on. We'll include details on supported transformations.
[05:02] Sara Patel: Network topology - if we do Private in our VPC, how does control plane connectivity work? Is there a backchannel to Redwood?
[05:10] Liam O'Connor: For Private we ship a control plane agent that can be air-gapped if needed. There's an option for a managed control plane with customer-managed networking where nothing goes out except optional telemetry. For Dedicated we manage the infra but we can set up VPC peering or private link.
[05:27] Dr. Marcus Velez: Is there any telemetry sent back to Redwood from Private?
[05:31] Maya Chen: It's configurable. You can opt-in for usage telemetry; for air-gapped installs telemetry is disabled by default.
[05:36] Priya Singh: On compliance evidence - will you share SOC2 and ISO certificates and also an SSAE attestation?
[05:42] Liam O'Connor: We'll share SOC2 Type II report summary, ISO certificate, and a list of subservice orgs. For detailed attestations we can coordinate an NDA if needed.
[05:52] Sara Patel: For onboarding, what does the procurement and contract side look like for Dedicated/Private? Any special terms for data processing or breach notification?
[06:00] Maya Chen: We have standard DPA language that includes breach notification timelines and data processing terms. For enterprise customers we can negotiate stricter SLAs and contractual controls. Liam - do you want to add the typical timelines?
[06:10] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated, typical procurement to go-live is 6-8 weeks; Private can be 8-12 weeks depending on network and security reviews. We provide a security questionnaire and can support ATO processes.
[06:22] Dr. Marcus Velez: Are there specific certifications for the infra - like SOC on the underlying cloud provider?
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: We rely on cloud provider SOC/ISO attestations for infra. We'll map controls in our pack so you can see responsibilities in a shared responsibility matrix.
[06:38] Sara Patel: Is there role separation for support engineers? We need to ensure access controls and just-in-time support access with audit.
[06:46] Maya Chen: Support access is role-based and requires customer approval for elevated access. We support JIT temporary access and we log all actions with session recordings for privileged ops.
[06:57] Priya Singh: Can we get more detail on encryption in transit? TLS versions, cipher suites, mutual TLS for private peering?
[07:04] Liam O'Connor: We use TLS 1.2+ and prefer TLS 1.3. For private links or peering we can do mTLS and mutual authentication. We'll add cipher suite details in the pack.
[07:14] Sara Patel: For SIEM integration, what formats do logs come in and what fields are included?
[07:19] Liam O'Connor: Logs are JSON by default with fields for request_id, timestamp, actor_id, model, prompt hash, token counts, status, response_time, and metadata. We can stream to your syslog, S3, or streaming endpoints.
[07:33] Dr. Marcus Velez: About the model life cycle - if you roll out model updates, is there a way to pin to a model version? We need deterministic behavior for audits.
[07:40] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pin model versions per route. We also support canary rollouts and A/B tests with audit trails of model versions used per request.
[07:51] Priya Singh: Are there guardrails or content filters for sensitive outputs?
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: We have policy enforcement hooks and content filters at the service layer, and you can plug in your own classifiers as a post-processing step.
[08:03] Sara Patel: If we start with Hosted for speed but later move to Private, what's the data migration story?
[08:09] Maya Chen: We provide export tools to move logs and model artifacts; for user data you can opt-in to have exported bundles. Migration planning is part of Dedicated/Private onboarding.
[08:19] Dr. Marcus Velez: Cost is also a factor. We want to weigh latency and cost tradeoffs vs compliance.
[08:24] Liam O'Connor: Correct - Hosted is best for time-to-value and lower operational overhead. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation. Private is the most controlled but requires your ops. We can run a cost/latency benchmark against your typical payloads as part of the POC.
[08:39] Maya Chen: Quick question on timelines - what's your procurement timeline for a POC?
[08:43] Sara Patel: We'd like to be running a POC in 4-6 weeks, internal security review in 2 weeks. Procurement can be 3-4 weeks after approval.
[08:51] Maya Chen: Great - we'll align materials. We'll send the SOC2 pack and a proposed scope for the POC.
[08:57] Priya Singh: One more thing - for data deletion requests, do you support on-demand deletions across logs and cached KV entries?
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support deletion APIs and permanent deletion workflows. For cached KV we have TTL controls and explicit purge APIs. We'll document exact behavior.
[09:15] Dr. Marcus Velez: About SIEM correlation - can you inject correlation IDs from our side into requests?
[09:20] Maya Chen: You can pass through custom headers and we persist them in logs. That will help correlation.
[09:26] Sara Patel: Sounds good. Any regulatory constraints we should be aware of from your side?
[09:29] Liam O'Connor: We support GDPR controls, data subject requests via the DPA, and region-bound processing. For healthcare use cases we recommend Private or Dedicated if you need full control of PHI.
[09:43] Maya Chen: Ok let's summarize next steps. We'll share the security pack (SOC2, ISO cert, pen test summary), the KMS/network diagrams, and an initial POC scope. Liam will run a technical deep-dive on networking.
[09:56] Priya Singh: Sounds good. We'll share our control matrix and retention policy after this call.
[10:01] Dr. Marcus Velez: Thanks all. We'll review the pack and get back with availability for the deep-dive.
[10:06] Maya Chen: Appreciate it. We'll follow up within 48 hours with the docs.

-- End of transcript --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings corrected; some proper nouns like KMS/HSM and KV cache sometimes mistranscribed as 'kay emm ess' or 'k v cache' in raw export. There was a brief crosstalk at 00:08-00:12.

References/shared artifacts mentioned during call:
- Security pack (SOC2 Type II summary, ISO 27001 cert, pen test summary) - to be sent
- Network diagram and KMS integration example - to be shared
- POC scope doc template - Redwood will propose
